chunks.title: Dilating drops & tetanus
chunks.tldr: Duration: phenylephrine 3 h, tropicamide 3–6 h, cyclopentolate 24 h, homatropine 2–3 d, scopolamine 4–7 d, atropine 1–2 weeks. Adults: phenylephrine 2.5% + tropicamide 1%. Kids >1 yr: any two of phenyl 2.5%, trop 1%, cyclo 1–2%. Preterm/neonates: phenyl 1%, trop 1%, cyclo 0.2–0.5%. Dark irides dilate less. Tetanus (toxoid 0.5 mL IM): <2 doses → toxoid (+ immunoglobulin if dirty wound); ≥3 doses → toxoid if clean wound >10 yrs or dirty wound >5 yrs since last dose.
chunks.hook: Trop = afternoon, Cyclo = a day, Atropine = a fortnight.

chunks.title: Cover tests, Amsler, Seidel, forced ductions
chunks.tldr: Cover–uncover (do first): movement of the uncovered eye = tropia; eye moves out → eso, in → exo, down → hyper. Alternate cover: total deviation (tropia + phoria), can't separate them; prism base toward the direction of refixation until movement stops; measure all gazes and head tilts. Amsler: 12 inches, one eye, central dot; red grid more sensitive. Seidel: concentrated fluorescein turns into a green dilute stream under cobalt blue = leak. Forced duction (anaesthetised, forceps near limbus): resistance = restriction; active force generation compares muscle strength (awake patients).
points: Eso: eye moves temporally to refixate; exo: moves nasally.
chunks.hook: Uncovered eye moves = tropia. Prism apex points to the deviation.

cards.q: On cover–uncover, the uncovered eye moves outward to fixate. What is the deviation?

chunks.title: Lacrimal probing & corneal cultures
chunks.tldr: Probing: anaesthetise, dilate punctum, #00 Bowman 2 mm vertical then 8 mm horizontal, pull lid laterally (avoid false passage). Probe/saline exiting a lid wound = torn canaliculus. Irrigate 2–3 mL; patient tastes it = patent; regurgitation/ballooning = obstruction; stop if tissue swells. Corneal culture: for ulcers >1–2 mm, central, not responding, or atypical. Proparacaine; scrape base and edge; slides first, then media. Routine: blood, chocolate, Sabouraud, thioglycolate; Gram + calcofluor. Optional: Löwenstein–Jensen (post-LASIK, mycobacteria), non-nutrient agar + E. coli (Acanthamoeba), Giemsa, AFB, KOH, GMS/PAS.
points: Fungal suspicion: deep scrapings or biopsy.
Flame-sterilise and cool the spatula between plates.

cards.a: Non-nutrient agar with E. coli overlay.

chunks.title: Fortified drops & intravitreal doses
chunks.tldr: Fortified topicals: cefazolin 50 mg/mL, ceftazidime 50 mg/mL, vancomycin 25 mg/mL, tobramycin 15 mg/mL (2 mL of 40 mg/mL injection into 5 mL 0.3% bottle), bacitracin 10,000 U/mL, voriconazole 0.5 mg/mL (1 mL IV 10 mg/mL + 19 mL water). Refrigerate; most expire in 7 days (tobra 14). Intravitreal (0.1 mL): vancomycin 1 mg, ceftazidime 2 mg (2.25 in Ch12), cefazolin 2.25 mg, amikacin 0.4 mg (macular infarction risk), amphotericin 5–10 µg, voriconazole 50–100 µg, clindamycin 1 mg.
points: Tap/inject 4 mm behind limbus (phakic), 3.5 mm (pseudophakic); aim for optic nerve; 0.1–0.3 mL sample.

cards.q: Standard intravitreal doses of vancomycin and ceftazidime?
cards.a: Vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 mL; ceftazidime 2–2.25 mg/0.1 mL.

chunks.title: Injections & paracentesis
chunks.tldr: Retrobulbar: 25–27 G 1.25-inch needle above inferior rim in line with lateral limbus, along floor past equator, then superonasally into the cone; wiggle to check not in sclera; aspirate; compress 2 min. Sub-Tenon: inferotemporal, 25 G 5/8 bevel to sclera, follow globe curve to hilt, aspirate, inject. Subconjunctival: tent conjunctiva, 4 or 8 o'clock. AC paracentesis: anaesthetic, speculum, povidone-iodine 30–60 s, 30 G needle on plungerless syringe, bevel up, over iris parallel to it, 2–3 s passive egress; antibiotic drops after. Fix the globe with forceps only if IOP <8.
points: Tap-and-inject: subconjunctival lidocaine, wait ≥5 min; convert to AC tap if dry tap.
chunks.hook: Paracentesis: over the iris, never over the lens.

cards.q: Where should the needle be directed during AC paracentesis?
cards.a: Over the iris, parallel to the iris plane, bevel up — away from the lens.

chunks.title: Angle grading & laser PI
chunks.tldr: Shaffer: 0 closed; 1 ≈10° (Schwalbe only, closure probable); 2 ≈20° (TM, possible); 3 20–35° (scleral spur); 4 35–45° (ciliary body). Van Herick: peripheral AC vs corneal thickness — 1 <¼, 2 = ¼, 3 ¼–½, 4 ≥1 (not a substitute for gonio). Spaeth: insertion A–E, angle °, curvature b/p/f/c, PTM pigment 0–4+ (e.g. C15b = narrow occludable; D40c 4+ = pigment dispersion). Occludable: <10° or plateau. YAG PI: apraclonidine + pilocarpine pre-treat, 3 or 9 o'clock (fewer ghost images than superior), Abraham lens, 4–7 mJ, crypts; pigment gush = through; steroid 4–7 days; IOP check; gonio 1–2 weeks.
points: Dark thick irides: argon pre-treatment reduces YAG energy and bleeding.
Indentation gonio reveals true insertion — written as (B)D.
chunks.hook: Shaffer: count the structures you can see (more = wider).

cards.q: Shaffer grade when only Schwalbe line is visible?
Preferred location for laser PI and why?
cards.a: 3 or 9 o'clock — fewer dysphotopsias/ghost images than superior placement.
